page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-48 is an Arm-based compute instance provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of system memory. Operating on the arm64 architecture, it provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, delivering 2.0 GB of RAM per virtual processor core. The instance includes dedicated CPU cores, avoiding multi-tenant resource contention at the processor level.

The instance does not include integrated local storage disks, requiring all persistent storage and operational volumes to be provisioned via remote block or network storage solutions. Similarly, it features zero discrete GPU accelerators and allocates no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning networking architectures must utilize private addressing schemes or external routing layers.

Given its 48-core Arm architecture and dense CPU-to-memory ratio, the hardware configuration targets compute-bound deployments. Qualitative resource efficiency is high for workloads optimized for multi-threaded Arm execution that do not require massive per-core memory capacities. Recommended workloads include distributed batch processing, source code compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, containerized microservices, and web application serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused instance powered by 48 dedicated arm64 vCPUs and 96.0 GB of memory. Designed with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio providing 2.0 GB of memory per core, this configuration prioritizes core count over vast memory footprints. The virtual machine includes no local ephemeral storage, meaning data persistence relies on external cloud storage infrastructure, and it includes no discrete GPU hardware or default public IPv4 addressing. The architecture delivers strong compute density for workloads compiled and optimized for 64-bit Arm execution. It is suited for parallel processing tasks, software build pipelines, CI/CD runners, container orchestration platforms, and high-throughput web serving environments.
